data.body:
LOOP ITERATION 13 — J9 IS UNBLOCKED. J10 [rebar:bb8c-8283-80c6-4052] closed certified (both gates,
no --force-close) and its close explicitly reported 'UNBLOCKED: bda8'. This is the first time this
ticket has been reviewable since the split, since review-plan fast-fails on a blocked ticket.

Applied the two staged advisories that were not yet in the plan, so this is ONE revision rather than
two:
 * OBSERVABILITY for the newly-implemented members. Not polish — SEVEN of the twelve have call sites
   that swallow Exception at EVERY invocation, and they STAY swallowed after implementation. Without
   an explicit criterion, J9 would ship the exact defect class it exists to fix: a DC write that fails
   and reports nothing. The AC requires a WARNING+ log naming the member and remote id, or a bridge
   alert.
 * validate_assignee_exists ERROR PATH. Testing 'the right REST call' is insufficient; its contract is
   the EXCEPTION TYPE. outbound_assignee.py:113 branches on
   type(exc).__name__ == 'AssigneeNotFoundError', so any other type silently downgrades every DC
   assignee resolution to the non-authoritative string-match fallback. 'A lookup happened' is not
   evidence.

The other two staged items were already folded in during the split revision (outbound_field_diff.py
documented as NOT a patch site; the _identity_of key and priority rule specified).

Plan is now 16 ACs / 8 files, down from 17 ACs / 10 files before the exception contract moved to J10 —
smaller in surface while COVERING MORE, which is what a good split looks like. Review round 9 running.

Also carried into this revision from J8's review: the transport-member count is TWENTY-ONE, not
fifteen. Re-measured — a call-form-only AST scan finds 15; counting every attribute access on a
client/transport receiver finds 21, because the reconciler passes methods as VALUES. J8 had the stale
number and now matches.
